about: What Spinach builds for the admin side, in one page: Spinach's own feature matrix (9 Jul 2026) with one column added, the version picked for launch and who provides it, one line why; then the six things Spinach builds; then what Zoho and the consoles hold (the details are doc 2); then the five open items; then Kajal's list of 8 Sep 2026 line by line, with where each line lands. The sheet is not the universal set: what sits outside it is in the folded notes and reaches Spinach only as B1 to B5. Picks proposed 2 Oct 2026; to be decided: confirm the picks.
cause: Vatsal, 2 Oct 2026 (the question: is the sheet the universal set; per row, which version and who)
rules: One way, app to Zoho: Zoho never writes into the app; the app may pull from Zoho when it opens something (H07 pulls the Desk thread).
Writes into the app by staff (edits to client data, flags, deletions, publishing) stay in the app; that is the whole reason a built surface exists.
Bands only in Zoho: no PAN, no financial numbers beyond bands; the record of truth for regulated records is the app's database.
The state is computed in the app and mirrored to the Contact; Zoho never computes a state.
A level is picked for launch; a higher level is later or never, and the reason says which.

universal.answer: No. The sheet is the generic admin universe of a consumer fintech app, written before the product model existed (the sheet is dated 9 Jul 2026, the v0.1 admin spec 8 Sep 2026). It carries nothing about the client's plan or financial record, the engine, data-quality work, DIFM onboarding, compliance records, AA renewals or deletion requests. Kajal's list of 8 Sep 2026 (the 48 placement rows on the Admin and CRM tab) covers that half. The sheet and that list together are the admin universe; the CRM set (calls, bookings, the pre-call view, nudges, tickets) sits beside it and is left for later here.
outside: The client record and financial data: one person's record with source and precision badges, edits on behalf, the engine re-run (own row 1).
Data-quality and ops work: unknown ISINs, implausible values, AA fetch failures with manual fallback, refund and reassignment requests, deletion requests (own row 2).
Assisted onboarding and DIFM provisioning (own row 3).
AA consents and CAS: expiry, renewals (S15), FIP failures, CAS uploads (own row 4).
Plan versions and the engine's master data: the logic panel L00 to L09 (own row 5).
The nine compliance records, their exports and retention; deletion under DPDP (own row 6).
Payments and refunds beyond a subscription list: a la carte receipts, GST, the refund flag (own row 7).
The returning-user states board with ladder days (own row 8).
The pre-call view, which borders the CRM set (own row 9).
The database KPIs (AUA, SIP book, AA availed, plans built, failure rates) are under the sheet's Dashboard row.
universal.crm_later: Calls and bookings (K01, K04, Zoho Bookings), the nudge matrix (Zoho Campaigns), tickets and the grievance register (Zoho Desk), call centre tasks (brief V2), DIFM prospects, consent and DND handling: the CRM set, on the Admin and CRM tab, not picked here.

v1: As an admin, I can view all registered users in a searchable and filterable list.
As an admin, I can view user profiles including registration details, onboarding stage, subscription status and account status.
v1_5: As an admin, I can view device history, login history, last activity, registration source, linked accounts and user lifecycle timeline.
v2: As an admin, I can activate, deactivate or suspend user accounts, reset passwords, unlock accounts, resend verification emails/OTPs and export filtered user lists.
v3: As an admin, I can analyse user growth, retention, churn, onboarding drop-offs, subscription conversions and user segmentation trends through dashboards.
why: A yeslyf user is a Contact in Zoho CRM: one per phone number, written at signed_up and updated by the event feed, app to Zoho. The Contact already carries what the profile asks for: registration details, the journey stage (the onboarding stage), tier and SKU, subscription status, account dates, last activity, source. The list with search and filters is the CRM list view; eleven saved views by seat exist in the trial (phase G3). Nothing is built for the views.

The enhanced views fall out of the same feed: last activity and registration source are mirrored fields, the lifecycle timeline is the Contact's App Events, linked accounts come from the aa_connected event (the institutions). Device and login history are not in the model and would put more personal data into a processor for no decision anyone takes; dropped.

The actions as written assume passwords and account states the app does not have: sign-in is OTP only (A02), there is no unlock, no reset and no resend (the person retries). Export is the CRM's own export. Two of the actions are real and are writes into the app: handling a deletion request (H09, state S25) and setting the DIFM tier. Writes into the app never come from Zoho, so they sit on the one built surface, the staff view of a client (own row 1).

The analytics are bought twice over: Mixpanel for retention, churn and drop-off by screen (every screen ID is an event), Zoho Analytics for growth and segments over Contacts; the five seat dashboards exist in the trial (phase G4).
features.zoho: Contacts with the mirrored fields (CONTACT_FIELDS on the Admin and CRM tab), saved views by journey stage and status, the CRM export, the App Events timeline, the Analytics dashboards.
features.spinach: The staff view of a client for the two writes (own row 1); the feed: signed_up with source and device, every state change, the mirrors.
verify: which state flags are mirrored, so the CRM list filters cover what the seats ask for (state, tier, path, adviser, flags, DIFM prospect)
decide: to be decided: whether a user account can be suspended, and by whom (gap G20)
to be decided: a devices and sessions tab (gap G24)
features.line: A user is a Zoho Contact fed by the app; list, profile and timeline are CRM views. V2's account actions do not exist in an OTP-only app.

v1: As an admin, I can view users with pending onboarding, incomplete registrations, failed KYC and pending Account Aggregator consent.
v1_5: As an admin, I can track onboarding progress by stage, identify drop-off points and view onboarding completion percentages.
v2: As an admin, I can resend onboarding emails, OTPs, KYC requests and Account Aggregator consent requests where applicable.
v3: As an admin, I can analyse onboarding funnel performance, conversion rates, abandonment reasons and onboarding SLA metrics.
why: Onboarding in yeslyf is not a four-stage funnel (registration, KYC, AA consent, profile setup) but the returning-user states S1 to S5, with KYC at P02 and AA at A06 to A09. The state is computed in the app and mirrored to the Contact as the journey stage; KYC and AA statuses are mirrored fields. So 'pending onboarding, incomplete registration, failed KYC, pending AA consent' are four saved views in the CRM, made by hand like the eleven in the trial.

Progress by stage and drop-off points (the enhanced views) are Mixpanel funnels: reveal (R01 to R09), paywall (R12 to P05), data (O02 to D10), with the time between first and last step. Counts per state are an Analytics tile over the journey stage.

The 'resend' actions are the nudge matrix: Campaigns journeys keyed on the journey stage send the reminders on the ladder (S1a to S5a), and a human call is a CRM task (brief V2). A KYC or AA request is not resent by an admin; the nudge sends the person back to P02 or A06 in the app. A one-off send is a Campaigns send. Nothing is built.
The analytics (funnel performance, abandonment, conversion) is Mixpanel. An onboarding SLA is not defined; nothing to measure yet.
features.zoho: Four CRM saved views (journey stage S1 to S5, KYC status, AA status), Campaigns journeys by journey stage, CRM tasks for calls, Analytics counts per state.
features.spinach: Nothing on the admin side; the app keeps mirroring the state and the two statuses.
verify: Campaigns is not set up in the trial (G6 waits on a person): the journeys and the weekly cap are unproven
features.line: Queues are CRM views by journey stage; resends are Campaigns journeys and call tasks; funnels are Mixpanel.

v1: As an admin, I can view platform KPIs including total users, active users, active subscriptions and onboarding statistics (upto 5)
v1_5: As an admin, I can filter dashboards by date, user type, subscription plan and registration source.
v2: As an admin, I can download dashboard reports and configure dashboard widgets relevant to my role.
v3: As an admin, I can view trend analysis, user behaviour insights, subscription forecasting and platform growth metrics.
why: Five dashboards, one per seat, exist in the trial over the CRM data (phase G4): principal officer, call centre, compliance, finance, marketing. They cover the KPIs that come from the CRM (users, paid by SKU, states, opt-ins, tickets, refunds); filters by date and SKU (the enhanced views) are dashboard configuration; per-role widgets are one dashboard per seat, done.

Twelve of Kajal's KPI rows come from the app's database, not the CRM: AUA, SIP book, AA availed, plans built and read, KYC and AA failure rates and the like. On 2 Oct 2026 they moved from Metabase to Zoho Analytics. Most can be fed as App Events or mirrored fields (plan_built, aa_connected and kyc_failed are events already); AUA and the SIP book need a monthly snapshot per Contact, which puts numbers, not bands, into Zoho.

Active users is Mixpanel (DAU, WAU, MAU from app_open); Analytics can approximate from last activity. The analytics (trends, forecasting) is the same tool once there is history; forecasting is not a launch need.
The sketches' dashboard (pages 2 and 3) is the principal officer dashboard plus three CRM views for the attention tiles plus the health page (B6) for system health. Nothing is built.
features.zoho: Analytics (the five dashboards, G4), CRM views for the attention counts.
features.spinach: The feed: events and mirrors; the monthly AUA and SIP snapshot push if accepted.
verify: how the app database reaches Zoho Analytics (the twelve database rows)
dashboard sharing per seat after G1 (the trial org shows no sharing control)
scheduled email and export of a dashboard
decide: to be decided: AUA and SIP book numbers per Contact in Zoho (the bands-only rule), or AUA read from a database export only
features.line: Five seat dashboards exist in Zoho Analytics already (G4); the twelve database KPIs follow the feed, to be verified.

v1: As an admin, I can create notification templates for email, push and in-app messages.
v1_5: As an admin, I can schedule notifications, create user segments and maintain notification templates.
v2: As an admin, I can trigger manual notifications, resend failed notifications and cancel scheduled campaigns.
v3: As an admin, I can analyse notification delivery, open rates, click-through rates, engagement and campaign effectiveness.
why: Templates and journeys for email and WhatsApp are Zoho Campaigns (bought), with the nudge matrix as their content; WhatsApp templates go through Meta approval. Scheduling is the ladder inside a state, segments are lists by journey stage, manual sends, resends and cancels are Campaigns actions. Nothing is built.

Push and in-app are different: no Zoho product sends into the app. Push text and in-app copy live in I15 and are read by the app; the app sends push through Firebase when the state changes. That is app plumbing Spinach builds anyway, not an admin screen. The sketches' template editor (pages 4 and 5) with Email, Push and In-App tabs is therefore two tools: Campaigns for email, an I15 form for push and in-app copy keyed by the slot ID (N-S4-72h).
The analytics: Campaigns reports for email (delivery, opens, clicks), the WhatsApp provider's reports (I08), the Firebase console for push delivery, Mixpanel for what people did after the nudge.
features.zoho: Campaigns templates, lists by journey stage, journeys, manual sends, reports; I15 entries for push and in-app copy.
features.spinach: The push sender from state changes; the I15 reader for copy; every opt-out flows app to Zoho (consent is mastered in the app).

v1: As an admin, I can manage FAQs, banners, announcements, legal documents and help articles.
v1_5: As an admin, I can preview content before publishing, manage versions and schedule publication.
v2: As an admin, I can publish, unpublish, archive or restore content and manage approval workflows where applicable.
v3: As an admin, I can analyse content engagement, banner performance, search trends and frequently accessed help articles.
why: FAQs, tooltips, disclaimers, educational content, videos, sample plan content, question wording, agreement template versions, banners and in-app copy are content the app reads at run time from I15 (Vatsal, 28 Sep 2026). The views are a set of I15 forms keyed by screen ID, so a tooltip on D04 is found under D04.

The enhanced views and the actions (preview, versions, scheduled publication, publish and archive, approval) are a published flag and an effective date per entry, which the app respects, plus a review step before a flagged screen's copy changes (appendix G, compliance review). Creator and the CRM both offer approval flows; to be verified in the trial, since no Creator form has been built yet. The choice between Creator and a CRM custom module blocks the API shape the app reads by.
Half of the sheet's 'content' is logic: adding, removing or reordering answer options changes the reveal maths, so structure is a versioned release (D5); only wording is content.
The analytics (what gets read) is Mixpanel: every screen ID is an event; FAQ and help opens are events too.
features.zoho: I15 forms per content type with published and effective-from fields; an approval step for flagged screens.
features.spinach: The app reads I15 by API, with caching; nothing else.
verify: Creator or a CRM custom module: approval flow, versions, API read limits
decide: to be decided: Creator or a CRM custom module (I15)
features.line: The app reads content from I15 with published and effective-from fields; wording is content, structure is a release (D5).

v1_5: As an admin, I can organise configuration groups, maintain version history and review configuration changes.
As an admin, I can manage master data, lookup values, financial categories and platform configuration values.
v2: As an admin, I can activate, deactivate or modify configuration values with appropriate permissions.
v3: As an admin, I can analyse configuration usage, feature adoption and operational impact of configuration changes.
why: Two different things hide in this row. App configuration (SKU cards and the fee structure mapped to Razorpay plan IDs, feature flags, the calls-included matrix per SKU and period, band placeholders, the DIFM threshold, copy slots) is I15: the app reads it, the principal officer edits it, Zoho keeps the history. The enhanced views and the actions are I15 forms with roles.

Master data for the engine (assumptions, the band tables and plausibility thresholds, cohorts and risk bands, the instrument universe and financial categories, market inputs, constraints, staging, publish, impact preview, audit) is the logic panel L00 to L09, already in the wireframes and built by Spinach as part of the app. It never goes to Zoho: it is the maths, and publishing writes into every plan. L02 already says the bands are fixed per field from the M2 tables, so they are the panel's, not I15's.
The analytics (feature adoption, impact) is Mixpanel and the logic panel's own impact preview (L05). M10, the config screen of 23 Sep, is therefore not built; it was I15 made visible.
features.zoho: I15 forms: sku_cards, copy_slots, feature_flags, calls_included, bands, difm_threshold, with a change history.
features.spinach: The app reads I15; the logic panel L00 to L09.
verify: I15 change history and version read-back
decide: to be decided: Creator or a CRM custom module (I15)
features.line: App config in I15; the engine's master data, the band tables and the plausibility thresholds are the logic panel, Spinach's build from the wireframes (B2).

v1: As an admin, I can view subscription plans, active subscriptions, renewal dates and payment status.
v1_5: As an admin, I can view subscription history, upgrade and downgrade activity, trial users and payment failures.
v2: As an admin, I can manually activate subscriptions, extend validity, cancel subscriptions or trigger renewal reminders where permitted.
v3: As an admin, I can analyse subscription revenue, churn, renewals, plan adoption and lifetime value metrics.
why: Money moves in Razorpay: payments, mandates, refunds, invoices; its console is the view of payment status. The app's Razorpay webhooks update the tier and billing state and write one Deal per payment into the CRM (SKU, amount, period, Razorpay ids, start, next billing, status), so plans, active subscriptions and renewal dates are CRM views; the finance seat's views exist in the trial (payment reconciliation, GST split, refunds, a la carte receipts).

The enhanced views are the same data: history is the Deals per Contact, upgrades and downgrades are new Deals, trial users are a journey stage, payment failures are state S12 and the payment_failed event.

The actions: renewal reminders are Campaigns journeys (SV7, the S12 ladder). Cancelling a subscription is a Razorpay action that webhooks back into the app. Manually activating, extending or comping a subscription is a write into the app's billing state: to be decided whether it is wanted at all, and if so it is an action on the staff view (gap G19).
The analytics: revenue by SKU and month is read in Zoho Books (the ledger) and on Deals Amount in Analytics; churn and renewals over Deals; lifetime value later.
features.zoho: Deals per payment, the finance views (G3), Books, Campaigns renewal journeys, Analytics over Deals.
features.spinach: Razorpay webhooks into the app and the Deal per payment (plumbing).
verify: how Razorpay payments reach Zoho Books
Books included in the Zoho One licence

to be decided: refund policy (D12)
features.sketches: navigation only (All subscriptions, Trials, Payment issues)
features.line: Razorpay moves the money; Deals and Books hold the record; renewal reminders are Campaigns journeys. Extend or comp: to be decided (G19).

v1_5: As an admin, I can view administrator activities, login attempts and user actions.
As an admin, I can filter audit logs by module, administrator, date range and activity type.
v2: As an admin, I can export audit records for compliance or investigation purposes.
v3: As an admin, I can analyse unusual activity, security events and operational trends through audit dashboards.
why: The regulated records live in the app's database (agreements, risk profile, plan versions, payments, AA consents, calls with input changes, deletion requests, resolved ops items), so the trail of changes to them is written there, one row per change, by the app and by the staff view's actions. That is the record of truth; it is exported by a job or on request (own row 6), in formats brief H6 still has to settle.

The compliance seat's day-to-day view (by module, by person, by date) needs no built screen: the app pushes each audit row to Zoho as an App Event carrying who, when, the record and the field names, not the values, so nothing beyond bands reaches the processor; CRM views and the export do the rest. Zoho's own audit log covers actions taken in Zoho; the logic panel's audit (L08) covers the engine.

Administrator activities on the admin side are the staff view's writes, audited the same way. Login attempts depend on the sign-in choice (gap G21). The analytics (unusual activity, security events) is later; Sentry and Zoho's audit cover the operational half.
features.zoho: App Events of type audit with field names; views by record type and person; export.
features.spinach: Audit rows on every regulated change and every staff-view action; the push; the export job of the full trail.
verify: record formats (brief H6)
decide: to be decided: the admin panel login method and MFA (gap G21)
features.line: The app writes the trail and pushes it as App Events (field names, not values); views and export in Zoho.

v1_5: As an admin, I can generate operational reports for users, onboarding and subscriptions.
As an admin, I can apply filters and export reports in CSV or Excel format.
v2: As an admin, I can schedule recurring reports and share reports with authorised users.
v3: As an admin, I can view business intelligence dashboards and compare operational performance across time periods.
why: Operational reports on users, onboarding and subscriptions are Analytics reports over the CRM data, exported from there; CRM views export too. Scheduling and sharing are Analytics features: to be verified in the trial (the org showed no sharing control; after G1 the seats exist to share with).

The sketches (pages 8 to 10) imagine a report repository with archives, export history and 'monthly transaction summary' PDFs per user. The repository is the saved reports in Analytics; a per-client statement is the app's own PDF (G10), not an admin report.

What Zoho cannot export is what it does not hold: the compliance records (signed agreements from the vault, KYC records, risk profiles, the advice register, AUA statements, the full audit trail). Those are exports from the app's database, run as a job to a store compliance can reach, in the formats brief H6 settles. No screen.
The analytics (BI dashboards, period comparison) is the five dashboards with date ranges.
features.zoho: Analytics reports and dashboards, scheduled email and sharing (to be verified), CRM view export, Desk export (the grievance register), Books export.
features.spinach: The compliance record export job; the Razorpay export is Razorpay's.
verify: Analytics scheduled email, export formats and sharing after G1
record formats (brief H6)
features.line: Analytics reports, schedules and exports; the compliance record exports are a job the app runs (B5).

v1_5: As an admin, I can create administrator accounts and assign predefined roles.
As an admin, I can configure module-level permissions and review administrator access.
v2: As an admin, I can revoke access, reset administrator credentials and approve privileged access requests.
v3: As an admin, I can analyse permission usage, inactive accounts and security compliance across administrator roles.
why: Three systems, three role sets, one principle: advisers see their own clients, ops sees records, the principal officer sees everything and publishes. Zoho users, roles (Principal officer, Adviser, Ops, Support, Compliance) and profiles (Standard, Finance read only) are Zoho One administration (G1 waits on a person). The logic panel has its own roles (L01).

The staff view needs only who may open it and in which mode (read, edit on behalf, scope to own clients): an allowlist of staff accounts with a seat each, revoked by removing the account. The enhanced views and the actions (create, assign, revoke, reset) are that allowlist. A roles screen with module-level permissions (M14 of 23 Sep) is not needed, because the surface has one module.
Zoho's own MFA covers Zoho. The analytics are Zoho's user reports; not needed.
features.zoho: Users, roles, profiles and MFA in Zoho One.
features.spinach: A staff allowlist with seats on the staff view's sign-in; changes to it audited.
verify: the trial's user cap (11) and plus-addresses for staff invitations
decide: to be decided: the admin panel login method and MFA (gap G21)
features.sketches: navigation only (Administration: Admin users, Roles and permissions)
features.line: Zoho users, roles and profiles; the staff view keeps an allowlist as part of its own build (B1).

v1_5: As an admin, I can configure application settings, notification defaults and operational preferences.
As an admin, I can manage feature toggles, legal document versions and support settings.
v2: As an admin, I can enable maintenance mode, update operational parameters and publish system-wide configuration changes.
v3: As an admin, I can review operational trends and identify configuration changes affecting platform performance.
why: Feature toggles (tiers live, the artificial wait on G01, the nudge cap, AA required or optional, the trial period), legal document versions (agreement templates with effective dates) and operational parameters are I15 entries the app reads at launch and on a timer; The enhanced views and the actions are the same forms with the principal officer's role. Notification defaults are Campaigns settings; support settings (SLA, categories) are Desk setup, done in the trial (G5).

Maintenance mode and the minimum app version (Spinach asked for a configurable minimum version, FE-71) are two more I15 flags; to be decided whether to add them (gap G22). Nothing is built; the app honours the flags. The analytics are not a launch need.
features.zoho: I15 flags with effective dates; Campaigns and Desk settings.
features.spinach: The app reads the flags, including maintenance mode and the minimum version if added.
decide: to be decided: maintenance mode and the minimum app version as I15 flags (gap G22)
features.line: Flags and legal versions in I15; Campaigns and Desk keep their own defaults; maintenance mode is one more flag (G22).

v1: As an Admin, I can view the connection status of KYC, Account Aggregator, BSE StarMF, payment gateway, notifications and analytics services.
v1_5: As an admin, I can review API logs, request history, synchronisation status and integration health.
v2: As an admin, I can retry failed synchronisations, refresh integration status and download error logs where supported.
v3: As an admin, I can analyse API success rates, integration latency, failure trends and third-party service reliability.
why: The app already writes one row per integration call (vendor, outcome, latency). Reading that table in six vendor consoles plus Sentry scatters the one question ops asks, is everything up, across six logins. One built page over integration_events answers it in one place: connection status and last success per vendor, failures and latency, the error log as an export, and a link out to each console where the detail lives (the KYC and eSign provider, the AA provider for FIP health, Razorpay, BSE StAR MF, the WhatsApp provider, Firebase).

Retry stays honest: a button only where the vendor call can be repeated without side effects (a KYC fetch or an AA fetch can, a payment cannot); where it cannot, the page shows the state and the person retries in the app. to be decided: the vendors with a retry.

Engine health sits on the same page, since it is the same question: data complete but no plan built (should be zero), build time, the plan-upgrade job after a publish. Kajal's 'plans in progress' and 'time from data completion to plan' land here.
Sentry keeps paging on thresholds; the failure rates for the dashboard still come from the failure events in Zoho Analytics. The sketches' system health tiles (pages 2 and 3) become this page.
features.zoho: Failure events for the dashboard's KYC and AA failure rates.
features.spinach: The health page (B6) over integration_events, with engine health; the Sentry hook; retries inside the app.
decide: to be decided: the vendors whose call can be retried from the page
features.line: One page over integration_events brings the consoles together: status, last success, failures and latency per vendor, error log export, retry where a vendor call allows it; Sentry still pages (B6).

own.pick: Zoho CRM Tasks created by the app, worked in Zoho; the fix itself in the staff view (data) or the logic panel (ISINs in L04); Analytics for the volumes
why: The queue is a list of work items with owners, ages and due dates, which is what CRM Tasks are, and the app may create them (app to Zoho); a refund request already creates a CRM task (BE-14).
